nodes.name: Sunlight and heat
nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives plant growth on the canyon floor, though summer heat and dryness limit it.

nodes.name: Scarce rain and snow
nodes.desc: The park is cold semi-arid, with about 413 mm of precipitation a year, so water is the main limit on plant growth.

nodes.name: Virgin River
nodes.desc: Its North Fork carved Zion Canyon, and the river corridor supports cottonwood, willow and boxelder along its banks.

nodes.name: Canyon soil and sediment
nodes.desc: Thin sandy soils and river-borne sediment give plants a place to root across the canyon floor and mesas.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Fremont cottonwood
nodes.desc: A riverside tree of the canyon floor that grows along the Virgin River and shades the streamside community.

nodes.name: Gambel oak
nodes.desc: A shrubby oak of the woodland and higher slopes whose acorns and leaves feed squirrels, mice and deer.

nodes.name: Utah juniper
nodes.desc: A dryland conifer of the pinyon-juniper woodland. Its berry-like cones are eaten by rock squirrels and browsers.

nodes.name: Prickly pear
nodes.desc: A desert cactus of the lower slopes. Bighorn sheep break open cacti with their horns to reach the moist flesh.

nodes.name: Desert grasses
nodes.desc: Bunchgrasses of the open desert and woodland floor, the main food of bighorn sheep and a staple for rabbits and mice.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: The most commonly seen large mammal in the park, browsing shrubs and trees. A main prey of mountain lions and a source of carrion.

nodes.name: Desert bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: Eats mainly grasses, with cacti, sedges and forbs when grass is short. Reintroduced to Zion after being largely gone from southwestern Utah.

nodes.name: Rock squirrel
nodes.desc: A large ground squirrel of rocky slopes that eats seeds, nuts and fruit, and is prey for hawks and eagles.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A small seed-eating rodent that is food for foxes, snakes and hawks.

nodes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
nodes.desc: Feeds on grasses and other plants at night and is eaten by foxes, hawks and eagles.

nodes.name: Gray fox
nodes.desc: A climbing omnivore that eats rodents, rabbits and fruit. Named as one of the smaller predators in Zion.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A soaring raptor that hunts ground squirrels, rabbits, mice and snakes from the air.

nodes.name: Western rattlesnake
nodes.desc: An ambush predator of mice, small rabbits and lizards across the rocky desert slopes.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever omnivore and the most recorded bird near Zion; it picks at carrion alongside vultures.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Finds carrion by smell and rides canyon thermals, cleaning up dead deer, rabbits and rodents.

nodes.name: California condor
nodes.desc: A huge scavenger that feeds mainly on large dead mammals such as deer. A pair nested in Zion in 2014, the first successful Utah breeding.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: The top predator in Zion. It prefers large prey such as mule deer and bighorn sheep, and its kills feed scavengers.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A powerful raptor listed among the park's birds of prey. It takes rabbits and ground squirrels.
